finding: Codex 0.147.0 spawns gpt-5.6-luna as a child and honours the requested model and effort, but offers that child no collaboration namespace at all -- only the three function tools. gpt-5.6-terra, captured the same way in the same run, is offered all six collaboration operations. The catalog's multi_agent_version field does not govern this: effective_multi_agent_version_for_spawn derives a child's backend from the parent thread and configuration, never from the child's model row (codex-rs/core/src/thread_manager.rs:1314-1333 at tag rust-v0.147.0).
limitations: Quality was not measured. `eligible-on-measured-criteria` means the collaboration criterion passed and nothing else was tested; it is not a statement that Luna produces good output.
Only the two leaf profiles are assessed. Any profile that spawns, messages, or waits on another agent is disqualified outright by the observation above, without needing a run.
The capture is per model, not per profile: two profiles sharing a model share its tool plan.

method.note: Codex is pointed at a local Responses API stand-in, so a real child turn is assembled and its model-visible tool specification is read from the outbound request without any model being called. Tool ABSENCE is therefore evidence from the tool plan rather than inferred from behaviour.
